One word many senses vs one sentence many parses.

recall.minute: NLP gets computers to analyse, understand and generate human language, drawing on AI, linguistics, psycholinguistics, cognitive science and statistics; it unlocks the knowledge stored in text and powers predictive text, grammar checking, search, assistants, spam filters, translation, QA, sentiment analysis, extraction and summarisation. Analysis proceeds through morphology, lexical, syntactic, semantic, discourse and pragmatic levels; sentences can be fine at low levels but fail higher ('green frogs' vs 'green ideas' vs 'large have green ideas nose'). NLU analyses; NLG plans and realises. Ambiguity is the central difficulty (lexical 'bats', structural 'visiting relatives', 'teacher strikes idle kids', the telescope PP attachment), compounded by non-standard text, segmentation, idioms, world knowledge and entity names. Preprocessing: sentence segmentation (beware 'Dr.', '3.14'), tokenisation, stop-word removal, stemming ('studies' → 'studi') or lemmatisation ('better' → 'good'). CFGs (rules + lexicon) yield parse trees; 'rice flies like sand' has two. Evaluate with task-appropriate metrics (precision, recall, F1) on representative data; tools include NLTK, spaCy, Gensim and CoreNLP.
